title: Commitment Fields: Risk, Meaning, and Constraint  Why LLM Weights Encode Absence
description: This paper argues that large language models (LLMs) do not generate output through probabilistic prediction in the conventional sense. Instead, they operate as constraint resolution systems in a high-dimensional, curved representational space. Tokens function as anchors that partition semantic possibility, while model weights encode the boundary conditions that govern which continuations remain coherent. Each output token is therefore not the result of temporal inference, but the collapse of a coherence field reconstructed at every step. This framework clarifies why LLMs can produce structured, contextually appropriate language without possessing goals, memory, or self-reference. It also provides a general computational analogy to biological cognition, where stable identity emerges from dynamic re-alignment rather than stored propositions. I further reframe risk management as the relational asymmetry between commitments operating under shared constraints, rather than as probabilistic forecasting or exogenous uncertainty. Finally, the paper shows how this constraint geometry relates to institutional and legal systems that maintain coherence under commitments, and explains why misunderstanding LLMs as agents leads to conceptual and regulatory errors.
